```{r doc-code, include=FALSE}
source("../code/R/doc_code.R")
```

All panels are produced by
[`script/Figure2.R`](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/immgenT-GP-analysis/blob/main/script/Figure2.R).
The code below is shown for reference (not re-executed on this page); the images
are its pre-rendered output. These panels quantify how many cells and genes are
"active" in each gene program, over non-thymocyte cells.

## Setup

Data loading (non-thymocyte cells), shared across all panels below.

```{r fig2-setup, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", c("doc:setup", "Load data")), eval=FALSE}
```

## (A) GP1 signature volcano {#fig2a}

```{r fig2a-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2A"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2a-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2A.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2A.** Gene scores for GP1, a baseline program capturing the pan-T cell
transcriptional profile. Each point represents a gene. The x axis shows the GP1
gene score, representing the magnitude and direction of gene regulation within
the program and scaled to a maximum absolute value of 1; the y axis shows mean
shifted-log expression across all T cells. The top-scoring genes are labeled.
:::

## (B) Active-cell proportion per GP {#fig2b}

```{r fig2b-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2B"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2b-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2B.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2B.** Histogram showing the fraction of cells in which each GP was highly active (loading greater than 0.1 in each cell), across all 200 GPs.
:::

## (C) Active-gene count per GP {#fig2c}

```{r fig2c-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2C"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2c-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2C.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2C.** Histogram showing the number of highly active genes per GP (genes with an absolute score greater than 0.25 in each GP, after per-GP scaling to max |score| = 1).
:::

## (D) Active-GP count by lineage {#fig2d}

```{r fig2d-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2D"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2d-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2D.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2D.** Box plot showing the number of highly active GPs (loading > 0.1) per cell across T cell lineages.
:::

## (E) Active-GP count, activated vs. resting {#fig2e}

```{r fig2e-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2E"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2e-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2E.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2E.** Box plot showing the number of highly active GPs per cell in
activated versus resting T cells. Unlike the other activated-vs-resting panels
in this paper (Figure 4, Figure S3), this one is **not** restricted to CD4 and
CD8: every lineage with an `annotation_level2_group` of `"activated"` or
`"resting"` is included, Treg among them -- which is what the caption's
"T cells" refers to.
:::

## (F) CD44 vs. active-GP count {#fig2f}

```{r fig2f-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure2.R", "2F"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig2f-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="50%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure2/2F.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 2F.** Scatterplot showing the number of highly active GPs per cell
correlated with CD44 protein expression (CITE-seq; log-normalized ADT counts).
The blue line indicates the least-squares fit; Pearson's *r* = 0.44. The
correlation is computed over all cells with non-zero CD44 (the scatter itself is
subsampled to 10,000 cells for rendering only).
:::
